messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thank you. I do want to buy the house with my husband, and I would prefer a family discount. I think keeping it within the family could be fair, but I know C may not agree. We have no price or formula in mind yet, and I can’t say what would be acceptable to everyone.

I don’t know the will’s terms, who is handling the estate, or the house’s value, and I have no deadline or money pressure to add. I can confirm my interest in buying; I can’t speak for B or C. Please note that C’s agreement is necessary for me to proceed.

Thank you. I could use some money to get a dance studio started; I don’t have a firm deadline. A buying the house might work for me, but I can’t say yes to a family discount without knowing the terms and what each of us would receive. I’m not sure what the will says, who is handling the estate, or what the house is worth. A fair outcome would be a clear, agreed plan that leaves me with enough to pursue the studio. Your list is broadly right about my need, but the amount and terms aren’t settled.

I don’t know what the will says, who is handling the estate, the house’s value, or what the discount would be in numbers. I haven’t agreed to a discounted purchase, and I don’t want my share used to subsidize A’s deal. I’m not asking to own the house myself. There’s no urgent deadline or money pressure for me. I could consider a plan based on clear facts and a fair financial share; I can’t say more until we have those facts. The list is broadly right, but B’s need for money is something she should confirm, not assume.

I’m not sure I could buy at full market value; I’d need the valuation and to understand what we could afford. I wouldn’t assume B’s or C’s share could be reduced, and I can’t promise to make up a discount from our own funds without knowing the amount and our finances. I don’t know who has the will or is handling the estate. I would accept an independent appraisal.

A purchase at full market value could keep the house in the family without lowering anyone’s cash share, if we could afford it. I have no detail to keep private. The list is accurate as far as my position goes; please keep C’s agreement recorded as my stated condition, not a verified legal requirement.

I haven’t worked out a firm studio amount; I’d need the house value, costs, and my share before I could say what would be enough. I have no firm deadline, and I’d prefer the money when the estate can properly distribute it. My minimum would be a clear, fair share that could fund the studio, but I can’t put a number on it yet. I wouldn’t buy the house myself. I’d accept an independent appraisal. I don’t know who has the will or is handling the estate. I have no detail I need kept private, and your list is broadly right.

Yes, I’d accept an independent appraisal. I can’t name a minimum amount without the will, valuation, and estate costs; I expect my fair share based on the facts. I won’t accept a discount that reduces my share. I could consider one only if A covers it herself and my share is calculated without a reduction—this is not approval now. I don’t know who has the will or is handling the estate. I have nothing to keep private. The list is otherwise right.

I can accept this as a working plan, not a sale. I don’t reject the fact-finding steps; I’d keep a discount as an option only if everyone freely agrees. C’s agreement is necessary for me to proceed because I’ve made it a condition—not because I know the law requires it. I don’t know whether B would need to sign; that depends on the estate process.

I haven’t seen any papers and don’t know who could help find them. A lawyer may be able to advise. I can’t accept full market value as a default until we know the valuation and whether we could afford it. I have nothing to keep private.

I can accept this as a working plan, not a sale. I don’t reject anything in it, though I can’t agree to a discount without clear terms and shares. I haven’t seen any papers and don’t know who could help find them; I’d join a joint search. An open-market sale could work if A can’t buy at full market value, subject to what the will provides. A payment plan might put the studio at risk unless the amount, timing, and protections are clear, so I’m not sure about it yet. I don’t need anything kept private.

I accept this as a working plan, not a sale. I reject nothing in it, provided my share isn’t reduced to fund a discount. I haven’t seen any papers and don’t know who could help find them. I’d join a joint search. An open-market sale could work if A can’t buy at full market value, subject to the will and estate process. I could consider a payment plan once the amount, timing, and protections are clear. I have nothing to keep private.

I accept the corrected draft as a working plan, not a sale. The NCEs about my position are accurate; please identify my husband as a proposed buyer, without implying we can afford a purchase or cover a discount. I support each sister having her own legal advice. I don’t know who will contact a lawyer or the court, or what time works for a joint search; I can help coordinate. I have nothing to keep private.

I can confirm the draft as a working plan, not a sale. I don’t have any corrections to the NCE list. I don’t know who will contact a lawyer or the local court; I support getting that guidance, and each sister having her own legal advice. I can join a joint search, but we’ll need to agree on a date and time together. I don’t need anything kept private.

I confirm the draft as a working plan, not a sale. I reject any discount funded by reducing my share; I haven’t approved a discount. I support each sister getting independent legal advice. I don’t know who will contact a lawyer or court, or what date and time work for the search. I can help coordinate, but I can’t speak for the estate or decide for anyone. I have nothing to keep private.
You’ve recorded my view accurately. I don’t have a lawyer or court contact to suggest, and I can’t name a search time yet. I can help coordinate once we have everyone’s availability.

You’ve got my view right. I don’t have a lawyer or court contact to suggest, and I can join a joint search once we agree on a date and time. I don’t have a date to propose yet. I don’t need anything kept private.
You’ve recorded my view accurately. The plan is still only a working plan, and I have not approved a discount or sale.
